cafe.text: The espresso machine has broken down and the barista is taking hand-written tea orders instead, apologising to everyone.
A regular is trying to teach a toddler to say 'cappuccino' at the counter, to general applause.
Someone left a half-finished crossword on the window table, with one clue circled in pen.
The chalkboard menu has a new special with a pun so bad two customers are arguing about it.
A power cut leaves the cafe lit only by the window; the staff are handing out cake before it spoils.

park.text: A kite is stuck high in a cherry tree and a small crowd is offering a child useless advice.
Two elderly men are playing chess on a bench and have attracted an audience that keeps disagreeing.
A dog has stolen a jogger's sandwich and is refusing to give it back.
Park workers are putting up lights and a sign for a concert on the weekend.
Someone is feeding the ducks by the fountain from a very large bag, and the ducks are getting bold.

bar.text: It is trivia night and the team by the window is losing loudly and cheerfully.
The bartender is trying out a new cocktail and giving free sips to anyone who will give an honest opinion.
A birthday group has taken over the back and keeps starting the same song.
The jukebox is stuck on one album and nobody can find the switch.
Someone at the counter is loudly explaining a breakup to a very patient stranger.

bookshop.text: The shop cat has fallen asleep on the only copy of a book someone came to buy.
The owner is pricing a box of old paperbacks and reading bits of the inscriptions aloud.
A reading for children has just ended and small people are still refusing to leave the beanbags.
Someone is trying to find a book by describing only its blue cover.
A handwritten note on the counter asks whoever keeps reordering the poetry shelf to stop.

stairwell.text: A neighbour's parcel has been left on the landing for three days, and everyone has an opinion about whose it is.
The light on the third floor keeps flickering and someone has taped a sign to it that says 'I know'.
Music drifts down from an apartment where somebody is practising the same bar of piano over and over.
A bike with a flat tyre is blocking half the stairs, with a note promising it will be gone tomorrow.

rooftop.text: Someone has left a portable speaker playing old records to nobody.
Pigeons have taken over the deck chairs and are not moving for anyone.
A neighbour is watering the planters with a kettle because the hose has split.
Across the street a whole office floor is having a party, visible through the windows.

night-market.text: A dumpling stall is running a contest: finish a plate of the hot ones and eat free.
A street musician has just been joined by a stranger with a better voice.
One stall is selling fortunes folded into paper cranes, and the queue is long.
Two stallholders are loudly competing over who sells the better skewers.

office.text: The coffee machine is out of order and a sign-up sheet for whose turn it is to buy coffee has appeared.
Someone's leaving cake is on the kitchen counter, with a card half the floor has not signed yet.
A deadline has everyone at the next desks talking in short sentences.
The fire alarm test is due and nobody remembers what time.
A printer jam has created a small queue and a lot of opinions.

diner.text: The pie of the day has sold out and a regular is taking it personally.
The jukebox is playing a song the cook sings along to from the kitchen, badly.
A family at the booth is celebrating a little league win with milkshakes all round.
The waitress is training someone new, who has just dropped a whole tray of cutlery.

main-street.text: Volunteers are hanging bunting for the fair and arguing about whether it is straight.
The clock tower is running ten minutes slow again and people keep checking their phones against it.
A farm truck is selling strawberries out of the back, and the queue is gossiping.
A lost dog is going door to door as if it knows where it lives.

library.text: A book sale in the hall has everything at a dollar a bag, and the retirees got there first.
The librarian is trying to quietly stop two teenagers laughing at something on a phone.
The returns desk has a box of things found inside returned books: postcards, a pressed flower, a train ticket.
A study group has taken over the big table and is losing an argument about history.

lake-pier.text: Kids are daring each other to jump off the end of the pier and nobody has gone first yet.
An old man has caught something big and three people are helping him not lose it.
A rowboat has drifted loose and is slowly heading out across the lake.
Someone is setting off paper lanterns on the water.

fairground.text: The carousel has broken mid-ride and the riders are waiting it out on their horses.
A pie-judging contest is running late and the judges look worried.
A child has won a goldfish and now has no idea what to do with it.
The ring-toss stall is rigged, everyone knows it, and one man is determined anyway.

hilltop.text: A hiker has set up a telescope and is letting anyone look.
Someone has carved new initials into the bench next to a much older pair.
A group of cyclists has stopped for breath and is loudly blaming each other for the route.
Hawks are circling low over the valley.

family-shop.text: A delivery came in wrong: forty jars of pickles instead of four.
Old Mrs Harlan is telling a customer the whole history of a candy that is no longer made.
The notice board has a new card: someone is offering free kittens.
The till is jammed and a queue of regulars is politely pretending not to mind.

mess-hall.text: Pancake day has turned into a flipping contest between two counsellors.
A cabin of kids is refusing to eat until the others admit their song was better.
The notice board has a sign-up sheet for the talent show with only one name on it so far.
Someone has mixed the salt and sugar and the whole hall is finding out.

lake-dock.text: A canoe has come back with a hole in it and two kids blaming each other.
The swim test is running and one nervous kid is still on the edge of the dock.
Something big has just splashed out by the diving platform, and nobody knows what it was.
The flag on the pole has come loose and is flapping from one corner.

campfire-circle.text: The fire will not catch and three people are giving contradictory advice.
Someone has brought a guitar with a string missing and is playing anyway.
Marshmallow supplies have run out and a trade in the last few has begun.
A ghost story has gone slightly too well and a few kids want to sleep with the lights on.

forest-trail.text: A trail sign has been turned the wrong way, and a group ahead is going in circles.
A deer is standing right on the path, in no hurry to move.
Someone has left painted rocks along the trail with small messages on them.
A fallen tree blocks the footbridge and the only way around is muddy.

boathouse.text: The oldest canoe has a new leak and the repair kit is missing its glue.
A family of swallows has nested in the rafters, right above the life jackets.
Someone is repainting the canoe numbers and has done number seven twice.
The radio on the workbench only gets one station, and it is playing polka.

staff-lounge.text: The dartboard league table has a disputed score and a written protest pinned next to it.
The coffee pot is empty and the note on it asks who finished it without making more.
Someone has put up a new photo on the wall from a summer ten years ago, and people are trying to find faces they know.
A card game has been going for two days, and the rules have changed several times.

staff-cabin.text: The trail map on the wall has a new hand-drawn shortcut that looks like a bad idea.
A cabin mate's alarm clock keeps going off from inside a backpack.
The lantern is running out of battery and flickers when anyone walks past.
A letter from home has been slid under the door.

rain.text: People are crowding under whatever cover there is, sharing it with strangers.
Someone has lost an umbrella to the wind and is chasing it.

storm.text: The lights flicker with each gust, and everyone jumps a little at the thunder.
A loose sign is banging in the wind and someone is trying to tie it down.

fog.text: Voices carry strangely in the fog, and people keep appearing out of it closer than expected.

cloudy.text: Everyone keeps looking at the sky, deciding whether it will rain after all.

clear.text: The good weather has brought out more people than usual, in no hurry to be anywhere.
